title: Solving Linear Inequalities in One Variable
student_objective: I can solve one-variable linear inequalities, reverse the inequality when multiplying or dividing by a negative number, represent solutions, and justify each step.
teacher_objective: Diagnose inequality-solving misconceptions at the first incorrect step, especially failure to reverse the inequality after multiplying or dividing by a negative number, and route students to targeted remediation.

concept_cards.title: An inequality describes a set of values
concept_cards.content: Unlike an equation that may identify specific values, an inequality usually describes many values that make a comparison true.

concept_cards.title: Keep equivalent inequalities
concept_cards.content: Adding or subtracting the same quantity on both sides preserves the inequality. Multiplying or dividing both sides by the same positive quantity also preserves its direction.

concept_cards.title: Reverse for a negative multiplier or divisor
concept_cards.content: When both sides are multiplied or divided by a negative number, reverse the inequality symbol. For example, -2x > 6 becomes x < -3.

concept_cards.title: Check a solution value
concept_cards.content: Choose a value from the proposed solution set and substitute it into the original inequality. Also check a value outside the set when useful.

concept_cards.title: Represent the solution
concept_cards.content: Use an open endpoint for < or > and a closed endpoint for ≤ or ≥, then shade in the direction of all values that satisfy the inequality.

items.tutor_behavior: If incorrect, connect inequality solving to maintaining an equivalent comparison and review subtraction on both sides.
If incorrect, demonstrate with numerical comparisons why multiplying or dividing by a negative reverses order.

solution_steps.explanation: Add 4 to both sides. The inequality direction stays the same.
Divide both sides by positive 3, so the inequality direction stays the same.
Check the boundary value: 11 ≤ 11 is true.
Divide both sides by -4 and reverse > to < because division is by a negative number.
Check a value in the solution set, such as -4: 23 > 19 is true.
Divide by positive 2; do not reverse the inequality.

items.prompt: Solve 6x + 1 ≥ 25. Give your first step before finishing.
items.tutor_behavior: Ask the student to identify the operation to undo first; do not reveal the full solution immediately.

solution_steps.explanation: Divide by positive 6; the direction stays the same.

items.tutor_behavior: Prompt for distribution first, then explicitly ask whether the final division requires reversing the symbol.
Score the first attempt and tag the first incorrect algebraic move.
Require a justification for the final inequality direction.

items.prompt: A student solves -5x > 20 and writes x > -4. Identify the mistake and give the correct solution.
items.answer_key: The inequality must reverse when dividing by -5; x < -4.
items.tutor_behavior: Require the student to state that division by a negative reverses the inequality direction.

misconceptions.description: Student divides or multiplies by a negative number without reversing the inequality.
misconceptions.remediation: Use concrete ordered-number examples such as 2 < 5 and multiply both sides by -1 to observe -2 > -5, then reconnect to symbolic solving.

misconceptions.description: Student mishandles negative distribution or reverses the inequality during distribution rather than during multiplication/division of both sides by a negative.
misconceptions.remediation: Separate the two ideas: distribute to simplify expressions first; reverse only when the same negative factor is used to multiply or divide both complete sides.

misconceptions.description: Student changes a term's sign without applying the same operation to both sides.
misconceptions.remediation: Write the same subtraction or addition explicitly on both sides before simplifying.

misconceptions.description: Student confuses open and closed endpoints or shades in the wrong direction.
misconceptions.remediation: Connect < and > to excluded endpoints and ≤ and ≥ to included endpoints, then test one shaded value in the original inequality.

misconceptions.description: Student performs earlier algebra correctly but fails at the final negative division.
misconceptions.remediation: Pause before the final division and require the student to name the sign of the divisor and predict whether the symbol must reverse.
